ratings.comment: Prof and course are both kind of bad. Lecture usually consisted of going over practice problems, but I felt that there wasn't enough coverage of the material beforehand - you would read the book to learn, and then go to class to practice. That works if you understand the material, but if not, you're out of luck.

Grieg is a great guy, but I have some advice for future students of his. On the first day of a new chapter in class make sure that you have (in this order): - watched the Learning Objective videos on Wiley - Read the chapter - Gone through Brief Exercises - Watched applied skills videos on Wiley - Gone through Exercises - Any worksheets he posts

This class is very challenging. Lecture is not helpful whatsoever and is almost useless to go. Exams and quizzes are challenging and it is often unclear what will be covered. Least favorite accounting class I have taken.

Professor Greig is incredibly smart but awful at teaching. I have taken him twice, once for 302 and once for 406. Both times were unbearable. His lectures are difficult to understand and unrelated to the exams. Grading is unclear--no rubric. I can tell he is trying, but it is just not working for him at all.
Greig rambles during lecture and doesn't teach about actual concepts in his assignments. Teach yourself and read the textbook to pass this class.

Tony is a very smart professor. However his lectures are very difficult to follow and incredibly dry. I would invest your time in reading the book over going to his lectures. His exams are also very tough, especially the problems.

Must be able to self-teach. Lecture is almost useless. Still need to go for participation points. Greig rambles or goes over 10Ks. Group homeworks are six in total, meet with your groups in person and youll do well. Greigs tests are fair as long as you read the book and practice the HW problems. Greig is a great guy in office hours

Try and take this class when Greig isn't teaching it- it'll save you a lot of headache. Lecture is absolutely pointless- don't go unless you want to look at random documents and hear him talk about New Zealand.

Professor Greig seems like a nice guy but his teaching methods are horrible. Lectures are disorganized, jumping back and forth from sample questions to discussing 10k of a real company. Exams are way more difficult than the textbook questions assigned.

Prof. Greig is a very nice and intelligent guy, but you'll need to teach yourself in order to get by in his class. He likes to spend the majority of his time talking about real-word issues and news that have nothing to do with the exams, so attendance is mostly a waste of your time. The group work in 406 is unbearable, so hope for a good team.

More of a guy who likes to talk and gives exams than an actual teacher. You will be teaching yourself ALL the content. Class is terribly boring. He rambles about irrelevant topics and can be rude at times. Quiz's are next to impossible, exams aren't as bad. Takes forever to grade things. Avoid his class, unless your on the Beta Board.

Greig was the worst professor I've had in the UW-Madison Accounting Department. I've heard in office hours he is very knowledgeable and likable, however, in lecture I found him arrogant and not helpful. You will need to teach yourself the entirety of the course material as lectures are not useful whatsoever. Avoid if possible.

Greig is a great guy, but a non-traditional professor. Class is spent reviewing 10-Ks and discussing pending accounting changes, useful info, but not like other accounting classes. Very little time spent on actual class material. Tests are challenging and based entirely on text. Wiley is Wiley, cases were not assigned, group presentations were easy

Grieg obviously knows a ton about the accounting profession. Are lectures boring? Yes. Do they seem irrelevant to the book? Yes. However, he spends time analyzing 10-K's and financial statements. It won't be on the test, but it is a glimpse into what accountants actually outside of the classroom fantasy.

Greig is no doubt a great guy and I want to believe he tries to be a good professor, but 302 is so dry and boring. Go into his office hours for any and all help, he's a lot better at explainingteaching 1 on 1. As for lectures... bring your laptop. Exams were tough, obviously, but fairstraight forward. Wiley homework is horrible, as always.

Class is not mandatory and pretty much a waste of time going anyways. Spends too much time talking about irrelevant stuff that won't be on the exams. I would recommend taking 302 with a different professor if that option is available.
Tony is a great guy, but lecture with him is horrible. It's extremely dry and confusing. Reading the book and doing problems on Wiley will prepare you for the exams better than going to lecture.
Extremely smart and very nice guy. Lecture is not really necessary and is pretty boring, though. He is very helpful in explaining topics when asked. Exams were very fair.
Very confusing in class but tests were relatively straightforward
Wicked smart. Helpful and open to questions
